answer: We model Sybil resistance as a ferrous commitment game where each identity posts dynamic opportunity-cost collateral calibrated to its extractable summit value, rendering identity splitting capital-expensive. Subgame-perfect punishment matrices impose slashing penalties exceeding any isolated island of deviation gains, while zero-knowledge verifiable delay proofs enforce non-forgeable participation histories. Thereby expected attacker payoff is strictly negative, anchoring honest identity uniqueness as the unique strict Nash equilibrium.
